title: node-ipc npm stealer/backdoor compromise
summary: Emergency denylist for confirmed malicious node-ipc npm releases containing an obfuscated CommonJS credential-stealing backdoor.

safe_versions: Use a maintainer-confirmed clean version such as 9.2.1 or 12.0.0 when compatible, and verify lockfiles before reinstalling.

commands: rg -n "node-ipc|9\\.1\\.6|9\\.2\\.3|12\\.0\\.1" package-lock.json pnpm-lock.yaml yarn.lock npm-shrinkwrap.json package.json .

detection_rationale: Confirmed compromised versions contain an obfuscated credential-stealing payload appended to the CommonJS bundle node-ipc.cjs.
The payload can execute when the CommonJS package path is loaded, so no npm lifecycle script is required for malicious behavior.
Reported behavior includes host fingerprinting, local credential file enumeration, process.env harvesting, payload wrapping, and attempted exfiltration.
The releases appeared across multiple major lines in a short window, which is a registry/release anomaly for this long-running package.
remediation: Block node-ipc@9.1.6, node-ipc@9.2.3, and node-ipc@12.0.1 in package-manager policy, CI allowlists, and artifact proxies.
Audit package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock, npm-shrinkwrap.json, node_modules/node-ipc, CI runner caches, and container build layers.
If an affected version was installed or loaded, rotate npm tokens, GitHub/GitLab tokens, cloud keys, SSH keys, CI/CD secrets, and developer-machine credentials.
Reinstall from a clean lockfile using a maintainer-confirmed clean version and purge compromised package-manager caches.
